hummler_1996_nat_genet.cite: Hummler E, Barker P, Gatzy J, Beermann F, Verdumo C, Schmidt A, Boucher R, Rossier BC (1996). Early death due to defective neonatal lung liquid clearance in alpha-ENaC-deficient mice. Nat Genet 12(3):325-8.
hummler_1996_nat_genet.verified_via: NCBI eutils esearch + efetch, full abstract, live this session
hummler_1996_nat_genet.numbers: alpha-ENaC(-/-) mice: amiloride-sensitive electrogenic Na+ transport ABOLISHED in airway epithelia (direct measurement). Neonates 'developed respiratory distress and died within 40 h of birth from failure to clear their lungs of liquid.' THE decisive genetic-necessity anchor for Claim B.

olver_strang_1974.cite: Olver RE, Strang LB (1974). Ion fluxes across the pulmonary epithelium and the secretion of lung liquid in the foetal lamb. J Physiol 241(2):327-57.
olver_strang_1974.verified_via: NCBI eutils esearch + efetch, full abstract, live this session
olver_strang_1974.numbers: Baseline PRE-labor fetal secretion phase: Cl- (and K+, Rb+) actively transported plasma->lung liquid (quantitatively the most important active flux); Na+ and Ca2+ move PASSIVELY down electrochemical gradient. Establishes the 'before' state that Claim B's labor-triggered switch (Brown/Olver 1983) acts on.

brown_olver_1983.cite: Brown MJ, Olver RE, Ramsden CA, Strang LB, Walters DV (1983). Effects of adrenaline and of spontaneous labour on the secretion and absorption of lung liquid in the fetal lamb. J Physiol 344:137-52.
brown_olver_1983.verified_via: NCBI eutils esearch + efetch, full abstract, live this session
brown_olver_1983.numbers: Gestation-dependent SIGN-FLIP: adrenaline slows secretion at 120-130 days, causes ABSORPTION after 130 days. Minimum adrenaline conc to inhibit secretion (Ai) falls from 0.43 ng/mL (132-4d) to 0.029 ng/mL (>140d) = 14.83x more sensitive. During spontaneous labor: plasma adrenaline 0.087 -> 6.86 -> 7.17 ng/mL (early labor -> last 50 min -> early postnatal) = 78.85x rise; noradrenaline 1.71 -> 12.14 -> 9.10 ng/mL = 7.10x rise. Adrenaline-infusion dose-response in NON-labouring fetuses reproduces the same switch, establishing sufficiency not mere correlation. Upper airway acts as a one-way valve (outflow only).

olver_ramsden_1986.cite: Olver RE, Ramsden CA, Strang LB, Walters DV (1986). The role of amiloride-blockable sodium transport in adrenaline-induced lung liquid reabsorption in the fetal lamb. J Physiol 376:321-40.
olver_ramsden_1986.verified_via: NCBI eutils esearch + efetch, full abstract, live this session
olver_ramsden_1986.numbers: Amiloride at 10^-4 M 'abolished the changes in p.d. and ion flux induced by adrenaline.' KI (50% inhibition of the reabsorptive response) = 4x10^-6 M -- applied concentration is 25.0x above its own measured KI. THE pharmacological-necessity anchor, decorrelated species+method from Hummler 1996 (fetal sheep, acute infusion, vs mouse genetic knockout).

hansen_2008_bmj.cite: Hansen AK, Wisborg K, Uldbjerg N, Henriksen TB (2008). Risk of respiratory morbidity in term infants delivered by elective caesarean section: cohort study. BMJ 336(7635):85-7.
hansen_2008_bmj.verified_via: NCBI eutils esearch + efetch, full abstract, live this session
hansen_2008_bmj.numbers: Aarhus birth cohort, Denmark, 34,458 babies, 1998-2006; 2,687 elective CS. Composite respiratory morbidity (TTN + RDS + PPHN, named explicitly as the outcome bundle) OR vs intended-vaginal-delivery: 3.9 (95% CI 2.4-6.5) at 37wk, 3.0 (2.1-4.3) at 38wk, 1.9 (1.2-3.0) at 39wk. Serious respiratory morbidity (O2>2d, CPAP, or ventilation): OR 5.0 (1.6-16.0) at 37wk. Results essentially unchanged after excluding diabetes/pre-eclampsia/IUGR/breech. THE clinical cross-check anchor for Claim B, disclosed as a COMPOSITE outcome (TTN is typically its largest component, not a TTN-specific OR).

overall_verdict.note: All gates PASS, but graded by decisiveness rather than presented as uniformly load-bearing (symmetric QC applied to a pass-heavy result, not just to a prospective kill). The PRIMARY claim (B, fluid clearance) rests on real measured necessity phenotypes across 3 decorrelated species/methods (mouse genetic knockout, fetal-sheep pharmacological blockade, human clinical cohort), not a simulated curve with invented parameters.

honest_gaps: The specific Karlberg-series installment reporting the actual first-breath pressure-volume loop numbers was searched for (4 query variants + a 118-paper title scan) and not located this session -- Part I and Part III of the closely-related series were found and bibliographically confirmed instead. The 40-80 cmH2O figure remains the task's own specified, textbook-transmitted magnitude.

The '1/3 mechanical-squeeze : 2/3 active-transport' split sometimes quoted in older secondary sources was deliberately not used or verified this session -- this cert relies on necessity evidence (removing active transport causes categorical failure) instead of a quantitative partition.

No standalone simulated 'passive-only predicted clearance half-life' was computed -- Part 2's adversary-forcing rests entirely on real measured necessity phenotypes (genetic knockout, pharmacological block, clinical cohort), not a simulated passive-only rate constant.

Hummler et al 1996's delivery mode for the ENaC-KO litters is inferred (standard mouse-phenotyping practice), not directly quoted from the fetched abstract -- disclosed explicitly, core necessity conclusion holds regardless.

The inverse-Laplace calculation assumes bare/unspread-film tension applies at the pre-aeration interface (same 50-70 mN/m bracket as the surfactant cert's bare-saline comparator) -- a reasonable but not directly-measured-this-session assumption.

Part 3's bulk-viscosity-ratio cross-check (36.4x) is explicitly NOT claimed to reproduce Hooper et al 2013's measured ~100x whole-airway liquid-vs-air resistance figure -- the gap is disclosed, not smoothed over.

Papastamelos et al 1995's chest-wall-compliance measurement was made in infants/children 2wk-3.5yr old, not specifically at the moment of birth -- the closest live-verified developmental data available, a disclosed extrapolation.

This cert does not quantitatively partition how much of the measured first-breath pressure is attributable to surface tension (Part 1) vs viscous liquid-displacement resistance (Part 3) -- both are real, decorrelated contributors; no claim is made about relative shares.
Meconium aspiration syndrome (task-named dysfunction) has no dedicated citation fetched this session -- this cert's scope is the aeration/clearance mechanism, not meconium-specific pathophysiology.
The Hansen 2008 OR figures are for a COMPOSITE respiratory-morbidity outcome (TTN+RDS+PPHN together), not a TTN-specific odds ratio -- disclosed as composite, not conflated with a TTN-only figure.
